description: Finger extensor mechanism, option (a) of the extensor-mechanism proposal: each extensor and band-inserting intrinsic keeps one actuator and one tendon whose path ends at a junction site on the proximal phalanx and continues in MuJoCo pulley branches (divisor = 1 / force fraction) to the central-slip and terminal-tendon insertions. Written into the right-arm XML by scripts/fit_extensor_mechanism.py.

r.meaning: terminal share of the force that reaches the slips

c.method: least squares (weights 1/SD^2) of the index EDC2 and EIP DIP and PIP moment arms, linear in c, against An 1983 (averaged over PIP 0-90 / DIP 0-60 deg, other joints 0) and Lee 2008b (mean of the nine postures); one c for every extensor
c.meaning: share of the extensor force that reaches the slips; 1 - c stays on the proximal phalanx at the hood (sagittal bands, capsule)

previous.where: Brook et al. 1995, Eqs. 12a-d: F_RB = 2/3 F_LU + ..., F_ES = 1/3 F_LU + ...
previous.note: EM-a values; the 2/3 terminal share gave the first lumbrical a DIP extension arm of 2.1 mm against 0.7 +- 0.6 mm (An 1983) and an effective 0.53 mm (Lee 2008b)

dip.where: Table 3 (LU; extension, averaged over DIP 0-60 deg)

pip.where: Table 3 (LU; extension, averaged over PIP 0-90 deg)

lumbrical.method: S5: both fractions solved from the two An 1983 arms of the index lumbrical with the model geometry (fit_extensor_mechanism.fit_lumbrical); the remainder ends on the proximal phalanx at the radial band junction (Eladoumikdachi 2002 II: bony insertion in 14 %, volar plate in 21-63 % of lumbricals); applied to all four lumbricals. The interossei keep the Chao & An fractions: their index arms (DIP 1.0, PIP 1.9 mm) lie between An 1983 (UI 1.6 +- 0.5 / 2.6 +- 0.8) and Lee 2008b (FPI 0.90 / 0.13).

interosseous.where: Brook et al. 1995, Eqs. 12a-d: F_UB = 1/3 F_UI + ..., F_ES = ... + 1/3 F_UI; the remaining third ends on the proximal phalanx at the band site
interosseous.note: kept at S5: the model's index arms (palmar interosseous: DIP 1.0, PIP 1.9 mm) lie between An 1983 (UI: 1.6 +- 0.5, 2.6 +- 0.8 mm) and Lee 2008b (FPI: 0.90, 0.13 mm)

dorsal_of_pip_axis_m.where: p. 1134: central band 7.1 mm dorsal of the PIP centre, lateral bands 5.2 mm palmar of it in extension
dorsal_of_pip_axis_m.method: 7.1 - 5.2 mm; also the radius of the band wrap cylinder coaxial with the PIP axis, so the bands stay dorsal of the axis (option (a) keeps their force at any flexion; Garcia-Elias: the bands that move palmar in full flexion carry little tension)

proximal_of_pip_m.method: band sites near the PIP head, where the intrinsic tendons join the bands (Harris & Rutledge 1972 p. 717: the bands leave the mechanism 1-2 cm proximal of the PIP, which places the junction on the distal proximal phalanx)

lateral.method: half the bone width along the PIP axis over the last 8 mm of the proximal phalanx (mesh), per digit; radial = +PIP axis

band_side_m.method: side site dorsal of the PIP axis for the band wrap

distal_band_site.method: via site on the middle phalanx just distal and dorsal of the PIP axis (radius from the axis, angle from the distal toward the dorsal direction), lateral like the band sites: the band leaves the band wrap there, so it wraps the cylinder dorsally over the whole PIP range (MuJoCo drops a wrap whose straight segment misses the cylinder palmarly, which turned the bands into flexors beyond 95 deg)

orl.method: One fixed tendon per finger over PIP and DIP, tension-only (deadband spring): length = r (q_DIP - q_PIP) with equal moment arms r = the model's terminal-tendon DIP arm at q = 0 (judgement: Landsmeer 1949 places the ORL palmar of the PIP axis and in the terminal tendon at the DIP; no source gives the arms). Slack = r x 30 deg, so it never acts in unresisted flexion with PIP-DIP differences up to 30 deg (Harris & Rutledge 1972, Table I). Stiffness fitted so that its share of the DIP resistance at DIP 45 deg, PIP 0, MCP 0 with 1.96 N on the extensor is Ueba 2011's 25 %; the total there is the Kamper 2002 DIP static torque plus the preload moment.
